packageRules.description: Routine patch/minor bumps arrive as ONE pull request a week, not thirty. Nothing here should need individual review.
Majors get their own PR each: these are the ones that break a build, and batching them makes the culprit impossible to identify.
The framework spine moves together or not at all. Next and its eslint config disagreeing on version is a known way to get confusing lint failures.
Prisma's client and CLI MUST share a version -- a mismatch produces a generated client that does not match the schema, which typechecks and then fails at runtime.
React and its DOM package are pinned exactly in package.json (19.2.4, no caret). Renovate respects that; this rule keeps them in one PR so they can never drift apart.
next-auth is on a 5.0.0-beta. Betas can change shape between patch releases, so this one is never grouped and never quiet: auth breaking is the worst failure this site has.
Playwright's npm package and its downloaded browsers must match, and a bump means re-running the visual baselines. Held a week so a bad release is yanked before it lands here.
addLabels: run npm run visual after merging

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes ignore the weekly schedule and arrive immediately.
